description:
Sitar to Unclog Your Brain | Indian Instrumental | 3 Hours

You don't always know what's in the way. You just know something is.

The week builds up in layers — conversations that didn't finish, thoughts that went nowhere, things you half-processed and put down somewhere. By Sunday evening the mind feels full in a way that's hard to name. Not anxious exactly. Not tired exactly. Just — stuck. Heavy. A little clogged.

This is 3 hours of slow Sitar in Raga Yaman — the classical Indian evening raga. Yaman is expansive and unhurried. Its phrases open outward instead of closing in. There's space in it. Room for the mind to gradually untangle from itself.

Three hours means you don't have to think about it stopping. Press play at 7pm and it's still going at 10pm. By then, whatever was clogging things will have had time to shift.

A gentle theta layer sits underneath at very low volume — not to sedate, just to support the mind moving toward a calmer state as the evening deepens.

🎵 What you'll hear:
- Sitar — warm, resonant plucked tones with natural sustain
- Raga Yaman — the quintessential Indian evening raga, expansive and open
- Slow tempo — unhurried phrases with space between them
- 3 unbroken hours — no restarts, no interruptions
- A barely-there theta layer underneath

⏱ Chapters
0:00    Opening phrases
30:00   Settling in
60:00   Mind beginning to clear
90:00   Deep calm
150:00  Still and open
170:00  Peaceful close

🧠 How to use:
Press play. Don't try to do anything with it. You don't need to meditate or focus — just let it be on. The Sitar does the work. You just need to be in the room with it.

⏱ Best for:
• End-of-week mental overload
• Mind that feels stuck or cluttered
• Anxiety without a clear cause
• Evening wind-down into sleep
• 3 hours of uninterrupted calm

suno_prompt: Instrumental only, no vocals. Slow sitar solo in raga Yaman, late evening anxiety-release and mind-clearing mood, warm resonant plucked tones with long natural sustain and slow expansive melodic phrases, no percussion, no tabla, 432Hz tuning, 45-55 BPM very slow tempo, sparse phrases with generous space between them, mid register (warm, open, resonant — not too bright), cinematic meditative production, expansive and gradually opening feel, suitable for extended looping in post-production. Raga Yaman tonic C or D — evening raga with raised 4th (teevra Ma). Emotionally: like the mind gradually unclogging and opening up — not sudden, just slow and inevitable. Each phrase feels like a door gently opening. Theta wave layer at -20dB very subtle underneath. IMPORTANT: Yaman has an upward, expansive character — the raised 4th gives it space and openness. Use this to create a sense of mental unclogging and release.

First Sitar use of Yaman (previous Sitar ships: Bhairavi May 26, Bilawal May 19, Bhupali May 11). Sitar warm resonant tone — brighter than Sarod, more sustain than Bansuri. Theta 6Hz for deep mental relaxation and mind-clearing.
